source_refs.note: 5. Paint Sprayer: a main subheading of 5.12 Uses of Bernoulli's principle, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 109-109.

blocks.text: A stream of air passing over a tube dipped in a liquid will cause the liquid to rise in the tube as shown in Fig. 5.21. This effect is used in perfume bottles and paint sprayers. Actually when the rubber ball of atomizer is squeezed, the air is blown through tube and it rushes out through the narrow aperture with high speed and it causes fall of pressure. So, the atmospheric pressure pushes the perfume up leading to the narrow aperture.

blocks.alt: Air, shown by a blue arrow, enters a line that narrows to a nozzle on the right. A vertical tube dips from the nozzle into a container of red paint; red arrows show the paint rising up the tube and being sprayed out of the nozzle. Blue arrows press down on the paint surface inside the container. Labels: Air, Nozzle, Paint.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.21: A stream of air passing over a tube dipped in a liquid (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.21).
